source: #1534 (what housekeeping refuses); RFC 0013 B2b (the runner's paths)
statement: No thread that calls the snapshot source writes a log line, or runs housekeeping's work, because housekeeping's queue is full: a refused log line, eviction pass under the cap or lag report is dropped and counted by its task (`HousekeepingTask`), and housekeeping itself writes one summary at most every 10 seconds, only when something moved, naming the last text dropped per task without its stack. Only the over-cap pass (SNP-14), an empty key's drop and the source's hand-offs (SNP-15) run in place. A meter that throws is counted in the summary's own state, never logged on the caller's thread nor offered to housekeeping, and the summary is written whatever the metrics are. Housekeeping stopped by close is refusal too, except on the source's own threads, where the task runs in place uncounted; close ends by writing what was refused and not yet summarized, once, on the closing thread, whatever the interval.

runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#a prewarm warning is dropped and counted
runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#a reset's line is dropped and counted
runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#a stalled pass's warning is dropped and counted
runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#housekeeping full across ticks keeps the family under its cap, and the late pass takes it to its bound
runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#a throwing refusal meter never reaches the caller, and the summary counts it
runtime:HousekeepingRefusalTest#nothing refused, nothing summarized
